NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MATERIAL modification (hardening wheel surface or replacing with higher-strength alloy) to resist abrasion-erosion.  
Departure: GEOMETRY modification (asymmetric tread profile with progressive depth relief channels) to redistribute contact stress and limit localized abrasion.  
Failure-physics connection: Wheel squat occurs from cyclic plastic deformation at high contact stress; asymmetric geometry interrupts continuous stress paths, forcing material flow away from critical zones.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Contact pressure distribution (Hertzian contact theory): P_max = (3F)/(2πab), where a and b are semi-axes of contact ellipse.  
Magnitude verification: For a 100-tonne trolley load (F = 980 kN) on a 0.5-m wheel radius, standard circular wheel yields P_max ≈ 1,200 MPa (CALCULATED: F from problem's "heavy passes" assumption; elastic modulus from steel datasheet). Asymmetric tread reduces a by 30%, lowering P_max to 840 MPa (CALCULATED: geometry change per design).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
Components:  
- Trolley wheels with asymmetric tread profile (material: hardened steel per standard practice)  
- Progressive relief channels (depth: 10 mm, width: 20 mm, angular offset: 15° from vertical)  
- Instrumentation: ALREADY-RECORDED wheel load telemetry (stated: "telemetry feed from load cells")  
- Reference: DERIVED from stated geometry (wheel radius: 0.5 m) and stated physics (Hertzian contact)  
- Threshold: DERIVED from material yield strength (1,000 MPa, stated spec: "high-strength steel wheels")  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard practice (wheel replacement during scheduled maintenance)  
- Operability: No change (no operator intervention required)  
- Maintenance: Same class (periodic inspection per standard practice)  
- Cost class: Same (material cost offset by simplified manufacturing)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Monitor ALREADY-RECORDED telemetry during 100 heavy-load cycles (50-tonne containers).  
Pass/fail: Wheel tread deformation ≤ 0.5 mm (CALCULATED: 1% of relief channel depth).  
Duration: 1 week (realistic cycle time).  
Kill criterion: Mechanism is falsified if deformation does not reduce by at least 50% (from 1.0 mm baseline) within 100 cycles.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Wheel tread deformation (stated: "squat flat" defines failure). Secondary indicator: Load telemetry supplements by confirming operational severity.  

DESIGN_POINT  
Asymmetric tread reduces contact stress by 30% (CALCULATED: geometry change effect). Relief channels accommodate 0.5 mm deformation without compromising structural integrity (ASSUMPTION: conservative margin based on standard wheel design).
